t: Mandela joined the African National Congress in 1943, moved from non-violent protest to co-founding the armed group Umkhonto we Sizwe in 1961, and was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1964.
Released in 1990 after 27 years, he negotiated an end to apartheid with President F. W. de Klerk and led the ANC to victory in the multiracial election of 1994.
As president he made reconciliation between the country's racial groups his primary task, while critics on the left and right, and later he himself, faulted parts of his record.
dyk: While a student at the University of Fort Hare, Mandela performed in a drama society play about Abraham Lincoln. He left the university without a degree after being suspended for joining a boycott over the quality of the food.
ev: Mandela helps to found the African National Congress Youth League and sits on its executive committee
He opens the Defiance Campaign at a Durban rally, is arrested, and is elected president of the ANC's Transvaal branch
Acquitted in the Treason Trial, he co-founds Umkhonto we Sizwe, which announces itself with 57 bombings in December
At the Rivonia Trial he is found guilty of sabotage and conspiracy and sentenced to life imprisonment
President F. W. de Klerk announces his unconditional release, and he leaves Victor Verster Prison on 11 February
The ANC wins 63% of the vote in the first multiracial general election, and he is inaugurated as President of South Africa
He retires after one term and is succeeded by his deputy, Thabo Mbeki
Mandela dies at his home in Houghton at the age of 95

f.born: 18 July 1918, in the village of Mvezo in Umtata, then part of South Africa's Cape Province; a Xhosa of a cadet branch of the Thembu royal family, son of the chief Gadla Henry Mphakanyiswa Mandela and Nosekeni Fanny
f.died: 5 December 2013, aged 95, at his home in Houghton, Johannesburg, after a prolonged respiratory infection; state funeral on 15 December in Qunu
f.role: Lawyer; national president of the ANC Youth League (from 1950); co-founder and chairman of Umkhonto we Sizwe (1961); President of the African National Congress (1991–1997); President of South Africa (1994–1999); Secretary-General of the Non-Aligned Movement (1998–1999)
f.known: leading the struggle against apartheid; the Rivonia Trial and the "I Am Prepared to Die" speech; 27 years in prison; negotiating the end of apartheid with F. W. de Klerk; becoming South Africa's first black head of state; the Truth and Reconciliation Commission; the Nobel Peace Prize
